definition: Learning a task from examples or instructions placed in the prompt, with no parameter updates.
details: In-context learning was highlighted by GPT-3: at sufficient scale, models infer the pattern from demonstrations supplied in the input and apply it to new queries. It subsumes zero-shot, one-shot and few-shot prompting and is the basis of “prompt engineering” as a practical discipline.

explainer.lead: In-context learning is learning a task from examples or instructions placed in the prompt, with no parameter updates. It matters because it makes prompt engineering a practical discipline and lets one model handle new tasks without retraining.

tiers.eli5: You show the model a few examples in your message and it picks up the pattern, like learning a game from a quick demo instead of practice.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers supply zero-shot, one-shot or few-shot demonstrations in the prompt to steer behavior. A pitfall is that results are sensitive to example choice and ordering, and no weights are actually updated.
tiers.paperLevel: Highlighted by GPT-3, in-context learning has models infer a pattern from demonstrations supplied in the input and apply it to new queries at sufficient scale, subsuming zero-shot, one-shot and few-shot prompting. Limits include sensitivity to prompt format and no persistent learning.

explainer.example: A prompt contains three example sentiment labels followed by a new review, and the model labels the review by following the shown pattern.

citation.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (NeurIPS)
